name: Daily cash pre-walk remains mandatory after Kyriba feeds automate
description: Lakeshore treasury must pre-walk consolidated cash by 9am Central even when Kyriba bank feeds are configured, because automated visibility is not the same as CFO-ready liquidity judgment.
summary: Daily cash discipline is a treasury control, not a portal feature. Kyriba improves visibility, but the Treasurer still owns same-day explanation of material variance.
doctrine: The Treasurer must pre-walk the consolidated cash position before relying on dashboard automation. Any cash surprise above five percent or any unexplained high-balance entity movement is reconciled same day and surfaced to the CFO before the next decision forum.
triggers: new bank or opco joins the feed
applies_when: The pattern applies whenever Lakeshore is using Kyriba or a similar TMS for multi-entity cash visibility across the holdco and operating companies.
does_not_apply_when: It does not apply to low-materiality petty-cash balances or archival account cleanup with no operational liquidity impact.

supporting_evidence.detail: Defines daily cash pre-walk and variance discipline as core treasury doctrine.
Frames value realization and early-warning controls as the buyer-owned success layer.
Live retrieval proof shows Kyriba Source and Move artifacts are accessible for CFO review.

anti_patterns: Treating a green bank-feed status as CFO-ready cash truth.
Letting cash exceptions wait until the weekly status meeting.
failure_modes: CFO acts on stale cash position during a liquidity event.
Treasury loses credibility because Kyriba appears live but unexplained variance persists.
embedding_text: Lakeshore Kyriba treasury success depends on daily cash position discipline. Even when Kyriba bank feeds automate cash visibility, the Treasurer pre-walks consolidated cash by 9am Central, investigates material variance, and briefs the CFO before decisions. This pattern connects cash visibility, variance thresholds, Source evidence, and Tower value proof for a diversified holdco.

name: Bank connectivity matrix clears before rollout confidence is claimed
description: Every Lakeshore bank, account, entity, payment rail, format, portal dependency, signer, and owner must be inventoried before Kyriba rollout confidence is presented to executives.
summary: Bank connectivity is a phase-zero readiness gate. Hidden host-to-host, SWIFT, BAI2, EBICS, or portal work can quietly become the longest critical path.
doctrine: Do not call Kyriba rollout green until Lakeshore has a bank connectivity matrix that maps every bank account to entity, feed format, payment workflow, signer, connectivity status, implementation owner, and sequencing priority. High-balance and high-payment-volume banks go first; tail banks are contained so they do not stall go-live.
triggers: bank feed is missing or late
Source event evaluates treasury rollout readiness
applies_when: The pattern applies to any Kyriba or TMS rollout where Lakeshore has more than one bank or operating-company cash estate.
does_not_apply_when: It does not apply to a single-bank pilot with no payment workflow or reporting dependency.

supporting_evidence.detail: Names the bank inventory and connectivity matrix as a Move 0 readiness gate.
Live Move attachment proof includes kyriba-rollout-gate-01-bank-connectivity-matrix.md.
Requires finance/treasury, integration topology, and vendor contract dimensions to reconcile.

anti_patterns: Discovering bank connectivity after design sign-off.
Letting low-value tail banks block the entire program.
failure_modes: Kyriba timeline slips while teams chase bank onboarding work that should have been phase-zero.
Payment control ownership is unclear for a connected account.
embedding_text: Lakeshore bank connectivity is a Kyriba readiness gate. A complete bank matrix covers bank, account, legal entity, payment rail, format, portal dependency, signer, feed status, owner, and priority. The pattern tells Sentinel, Nexus, Source, and Tower not to accept rollout confidence until high-balance and high-payment banks are sequenced and tail banks are contained.

name: ERP feed quality scorecard is the reconciliation gate
description: Kyriba implementation should not proceed on optimistic feed assumptions; Lakeshore needs an ERP, AP, AR, and GL feed scorecard with owners, defect severity, variance thresholds, and remediation sequence.
summary: Treasury transformation fails when ERP data quality is discovered late. Feed quality must be scored before reconciliation and forecasting claims are accepted.
doctrine: Create a feed-quality scorecard for every ERP, AP, AR, GL, and bank-position feed that Kyriba depends on. Each feed gets an owner, timeliness score, completeness score, mapping status, variance tolerance, known defect list, and remediation date before the CFO accepts the program status.
triggers: GL to cash reconciliation defects appear
opco uses a different ERP instance
applies_when: The pattern applies to Lakeshore's multi-opco finance estate where treasury value depends on clean ERP and working-capital data.
does_not_apply_when: It does not apply to a standalone reporting demo that explicitly excludes reconciliation, forecasting, and value proof.
decision_owner: Controller with Treasurer and ERP integration lead

supporting_evidence.detail: Frames ERP, AP, AR, and GL feeds as required readiness gates.
Live Move attachment proof includes kyriba-rollout-gate-02-erp-feed-quality-scorecard.md.
Requires apps, integrations, finance, and KPI rows to cross-reference.

anti_patterns: Treating ERP connectivity as a technical task with no finance owner.
Accepting forecast AI pilots before reconciliation defects are understood.
failure_modes: Cash forecast variance is blamed on AI when the underlying feed is incomplete.
Finance rejects Kyriba dashboards because GL and bank positions do not reconcile.
embedding_text: Lakeshore ERP feed quality is a Kyriba rollout gate. The scorecard maps ERP, AP, AR, GL, and bank feeds to owners, completeness, timeliness, mapping status, defects, variance thresholds, and remediation dates. It keeps AbarVa from making AI forecasting or value claims before finance data is reconciled.

name: Entity hierarchy and account registry prevent treasury misclassification
description: Lakeshore needs a canonical entity, bank account, signer, intercompany, currency, and operating-company registry before Kyriba structures are loaded.
summary: A diversified holdco cannot rely on casual entity mapping. Treasury, tax, control, and intercompany views must agree before Kyriba becomes a control plane.
doctrine: Load Kyriba only after the canonical registry reconciles legal entity, opco, bank account, signer, currency, purpose, intercompany relationship, and reporting hierarchy. Any mismatch between treasury, tax, corporate secretary, or controller views is a blocker for production reporting.
triggers: bank account is mapped to an opco
new acquisition or opco is added
applies_when: The pattern applies to Lakeshore's holdco and operating-company structure where one treasury platform spans several legal and operating views.
does_not_apply_when: It does not apply to a sandbox demo using dummy entities with no accounting, payment, or covenant implication.
decision_owner: Controller and Treasurer, reviewed by Counsel/Tax

supporting_evidence.detail: Names canonical entity and account hierarchy as a Move 0 gate.
Live Move attachment proof includes kyriba-rollout-gate-03-entity-hierarchy-registry.md.

anti_patterns: Letting implementation teams infer legal hierarchy from application owner names.
Treating signer data as a post-go-live cleanup item.
failure_modes: Cash is reported under the wrong entity or opco.
Intercompany balances and payment authorities are misclassified.
embedding_text: Lakeshore entity hierarchy and bank account registry are prerequisites for Kyriba. The registry ties legal entity, opco, bank account, signer, currency, purpose, intercompany relationship, and reporting hierarchy. The pattern prevents cash misclassification, payment authority gaps, and intercompany reconciliation errors.

name: Historical cash reconstruction is required before forecasting value claims
description: Kyriba forecast and AI-on-treasury claims are not credible until Lakeshore reconstructs enough historical bank, ERP, and working-capital data to establish baselines and error rates.
summary: Forecasting value is earned through clean history. AbarVa should distinguish future AI potential from finance-attested cash history.
doctrine: Before claiming forecast improvement, reconstruct historical cash position, bank statement, AR, AP, and working-capital data over a sufficient lookback period. Finance must attest baseline error rates, cycle time, and value assumptions before AbarVa or Kyriba claims AI-enabled improvement.
triggers: AI-on-Kyriba claim appears in a business case
CFO asks for value realization proof
applies_when: The pattern applies whenever Lakeshore wants to claim forecasting, liquidity planning, working-capital, or AI value from Kyriba data.
does_not_apply_when: It does not apply to a non-value demo that only shows navigation or workflow state without performance claims.
decision_owner: CFO with Treasurer and FP&A lead

supporting_evidence.detail: Defines value-realization tracking across forecast accuracy and working-capital metrics.
Live Move attachment proof includes kyriba-rollout-gate-04-historical-cash-reconstruction-plan.md.

anti_patterns: Presenting AI forecasting savings before finance attests the baseline.
Training a model on partial or unreconciled cash history.
failure_modes: The board discounts the value case because baseline and realized improvement are not defensible.
Forecast quality is weak because history is sparse or polluted.
embedding_text: Lakeshore cash forecasting and AI value claims require historical cash reconstruction. The pattern requires bank, ERP, AR, AP, and working-capital history, baseline forecast error, cycle-time metrics, and finance attestation before AbarVa describes Kyriba forecasting value as more than projected.

name: Intercompany reconciliation controls are Wave 1, not aftercare
description: For Lakeshore, intercompany lending, true-ups, interest, eliminations, and entity ownership must be governed inside the Kyriba success program rather than left as manual month-end work.
summary: Intercompany is a treasury control lane. If it stays manual, Kyriba may improve visibility while month-end risk remains untouched.
doctrine: Kyriba Wave 1 must include intercompany reconciliation design: lending terms, entity pairings, interest treatment, true-up cadence, posting ownership, exception thresholds, and close-calendar integration. Manual intercompany cleanup after go-live is a risk acceptance decision, not a default.
triggers: month-end close depends on treasury true-ups
applies_when: The pattern applies to holdco treasury programs with operating-company loans, shared cash, or related-party settlements.
does_not_apply_when: It does not apply where Lakeshore has no intercompany balances or the scope is explicitly limited to read-only bank reporting.
decision_owner: Controller with Treasurer and Tax/Counsel review

supporting_evidence.detail: Names intercompany controls as a Kyriba failure mode and readiness gate.
Live Move attachment proof includes kyriba-rollout-gate-06-intercompany-reconciliation-control.md.

anti_patterns: Leaving intercompany true-ups in spreadsheets after Kyriba goes live.
Ignoring tax/counsel review for related-party cash movement.
failure_modes: Manual month-end journals persist despite the treasury platform rollout.
Related-party transactions become audit and tax exposure.
embedding_text: Lakeshore intercompany reconciliation is a Kyriba Wave 1 control, not aftercare. The doctrine covers lending terms, entity pairings, interest, true-ups, close calendar, exception thresholds, controller ownership, and tax/counsel review. It prevents the treasury rollout from leaving month-end reconciliation manual.

name: Adoption and Excel elimination are measured controls
description: A Kyriba rollout succeeds only if Lakeshore measures role-based adoption and deliberately retires shadow treasury workbooks, not merely trains users once.
summary: Adoption is a control metric. AbarVa should show whether users changed behavior, which Excel processes remain, and who owns elimination.
doctrine: Every Kyriba role gets a usage expectation, training requirement, workflow owner, and Excel-retirement target. Adoption reporting must track actual workflow use, unresolved workbook dependencies, sentiment, and exceptions by role for at least the first two quarters after go-live.
triggers: CFO asks whether value has landed
applies_when: The pattern applies to all Lakeshore treasury users and opco finance teams affected by Kyriba workflows.
does_not_apply_when: It does not apply to a read-only executive dashboard pilot with no behavior-change objective.
decision_owner: Transformation sponsor with Treasurer and Change lead

supporting_evidence.detail: Names adoption and change tracking as a core AbarVa success-platform mechanism.
Live Move attachment proof includes kyriba-rollout-gate-05-adoption-excel-elimination-plan.md.

anti_patterns: Counting training attendance as adoption.
Allowing treasury to keep the old workbook as the system of record.
failure_modes: Users quietly return to Excel and Kyriba becomes reporting decoration.
Value realization stalls because workflow behavior did not change.
embedding_text: Lakeshore Kyriba adoption must be measured. Role-based adoption, workflow use, training completion, workbook retirement, sentiment, and exceptions show whether treasury changed behavior. This pattern prevents AbarVa from treating training as success or claiming value while Excel remains the system of record.

name: Covenant forecasting must run ahead of quarterly tests
description: Lakeshore should use Kyriba and finance data to forecast covenant headroom twelve weeks ahead, not discover leverage or fixed-charge issues near the quarterly test date.
summary: Covenant management is an early-warning discipline. Treasury value includes giving the CFO time to act before covenant pressure becomes a board surprise.
doctrine: Treasury and FP&A must forecast covenant headroom at least twelve weeks before test dates, using finance-attested EBITDA, debt, cash, interest, and fixed-charge assumptions. AbarVa should flag projected covenant pressure as a decision item, not bury it in dashboard commentary.
triggers: cash or interest rate assumptions change
applies_when: The pattern applies where Lakeshore has debt facilities, covenant tests, acquisition financing, or material credit agreements.
does_not_apply_when: It does not apply to entities with no covenants, no debt, or immaterial facilities not tied to treasury decisions.
decision_owner: CFO with Treasurer and FP&A lead

supporting_evidence.detail: Identifies covenant headroom as a treasury pattern and buyer-safe discussion point.
Positions AbarVa as early-warning and value-realization layer over rollout outcomes.

anti_patterns: Checking covenants only at quarter-end close.
Using unaudited EBITDA or stale debt balances in headroom reporting.
failure_modes: CFO has no time to act before covenant pressure becomes visible.
Board confidence drops because treasury risks were not surfaced early.
embedding_text: Lakeshore covenant forecasting is an early-warning treasury pattern. Kyriba and finance data should support twelve-week headroom forecasts across leverage, fixed-charge, interest coverage, EBITDA, debt, cash, and assumptions. AbarVa turns projected pressure into a decision item for CFO and board review.

name: Payment approval and BEC controls are rollout acceptance criteria
description: Kyriba payment workflows must be accepted only when Lakeshore proves segregation of duties, callback rules, new-payee controls, threshold approvals, and BEC escalation paths.
summary: Payment controls are not a checklist after go-live. They are acceptance criteria for treasury workflow safety.
doctrine: Before Kyriba payment workflows are accepted, Lakeshore must test segregation of duties, first-time payee callback, approval thresholds, signer authority, emergency-payment process, BEC escalation, and audit logging. Exceptions require named risk acceptance by CFO or Controller.
triggers: bank account signer data is updated
applies_when: The pattern applies whenever Kyriba or connected banks initiate, approve, release, or report payments.
does_not_apply_when: It does not apply to read-only bank balance feeds with no payment initiation or approval function.
decision_owner: Controller with Treasurer and Security/Risk lead

supporting_evidence.detail: Names BEC controls and payment workflows as treasury failure-mode content.
Requires security, risk, compliance, vendor contracts, and finance/treasury dimensions.

anti_patterns: Assuming bank portal controls survive unchanged after TMS workflow changes.
Treating callback verification as policy text without UAT proof.
failure_modes: Payment fraud exposure increases during a system transition.
Audit cannot reconstruct who approved a high-risk payment.
embedding_text: Lakeshore Kyriba payment workflow acceptance requires proof of segregation of duties, callback verification, approval thresholds, signer authority, emergency payments, BEC escalation, and audit logs. The pattern makes payment control safety a rollout gate for Controller, Treasurer, Security, and Risk.

name: Value realization scorecard separates projected from realized treasury value
description: AbarVa should keep Lakeshore Kyriba value claims defensible by separating baseline, projected value, committed benefits, and realized CFO-attested outcomes.
summary: The scorecard prevents the demo from overclaiming. Realized value appears only after baseline, intervention, and finance attestation are present.
doctrine: Tower and Moves must separate projected, committed, negotiated, and realized value. Treasury value is realized only when the baseline is finance-attested, the intervention is recorded, the measurement window is defined, and the CFO or delegate signs the result.
applies_when: The pattern applies to Lakeshore Kyriba, banking consolidation, working-capital, forecasting, payment-control, and adoption value claims.
does_not_apply_when: It does not apply to qualitative risk-reduction statements that are explicitly labeled as unquantified.

supporting_evidence.detail: Defines value-realization tracking across treasury KPIs and post-go-live outcomes.
Live Tower and Moves proof passed while avoiding realized value overclaim.
Source artifacts and Move attachments are retrievable for evidence-backed value review.

anti_patterns: Showing projected value as realized savings.
Counting a recommendation as a benefit before CFO attestation.
failure_modes: Buyer loses trust because AbarVa appears to inflate ROI.
Board value ledger cannot be audited.
embedding_text: Lakeshore value realization for Kyriba must separate projected, committed, negotiated, and realized value. AbarVa only treats value as realized after baseline, intervention record, measurement window, and CFO attestation exist. This pattern protects the buyer proof from overclaiming and connects Source, Moves, and Tower.

name: SI scope change control protects the buyer during implementation
description: AbarVa should make Kyriba SI governance explicit: outcome-tied milestones, change-control thresholds, named decision rights, acceptance evidence, and escalation paths.
summary: Implementation partner status is not buyer truth. AbarVa keeps scope, acceptance, and value gates visible so Lakeshore can manage the SI without running the SI's project.
doctrine: Every Kyriba SI milestone should have a buyer-owned outcome, acceptance evidence, change-control rule, and escalation owner. Scope additions, data migration deferrals, customization decisions, and training reductions require explicit CFO/CIO decision rather than informal project-team drift.
applies_when: The pattern applies when Lakeshore uses an external implementation partner for Kyriba or any major finance platform rollout.
does_not_apply_when: It does not apply to internal-only configuration changes with no vendor milestone, scope, or acceptance implication.
decision_owner: VP Innovation/Delivery with CFO/CIO steering committee

supporting_evidence.detail: Identifies SI incentive misalignment, scope creep, optimistic status, and go-live-and-leave as watch-outs.
Live Source artifacts are available for commercial-readiness and decision review.

anti_patterns: Letting the SI define success only as go-live.
Approving customization without future upgrade and control impact.
failure_modes: Scope creep inflates cost while value gates remain unclear.
Partner reports green until defects become executive issues.
embedding_text: Lakeshore Kyriba SI governance requires buyer-owned milestones, acceptance evidence, change control, escalation, and outcome gates. AbarVa is the independent success layer, not the SI. This pattern protects against scope creep, over-customization, optimistic status, and go-live-and-leave behavior.

name: Banking consolidation Source event should precede automation of fragmentation
description: If Lakeshore discovers fragmented banking during Kyriba readiness, AbarVa should create or update a Source event for banking consolidation rather than simply automating the current estate.
summary: Treasury modernization should reduce avoidable complexity. Kyriba readiness often exposes a commercial sourcing opportunity around banks, services, fees, and connectivity.
doctrine: When the bank connectivity matrix shows redundant relationships, high fees, fragmented services, or weak connectivity readiness, Source should evaluate banking consolidation or service rationalization before Kyriba automates the messy estate. The decision fork is containment for go-live versus broader consolidation for value.
applies_when: The pattern applies when Lakeshore has several banks, overlapping services, and enough implementation runway to evaluate consolidation without blocking critical cash visibility.
does_not_apply_when: It does not apply when a regulatory, customer, trust, or opco constraint requires the bank relationship to remain separate.
decision_owner: Treasurer with CFO and Source owner

supporting_evidence.detail: Identifies banking consolidation as a Source event triggered by Move 0 architecture.
Defines Source and Kyriba rollout as linked tenant demo surfaces.

anti_patterns: Automating a fragmented banking estate without asking whether the estate should shrink.
Letting consolidation analysis delay critical high-balance bank visibility.
failure_modes: Lakeshore pays to automate avoidable banking complexity.
The Kyriba implementation absorbs fee, account, and service fragmentation instead of reducing it.
embedding_text: Lakeshore banking consolidation is a Source opportunity triggered by Kyriba readiness. If the bank connectivity matrix shows redundant banks, fees, fragmented services, or weak connectivity, Source should evaluate consolidation before automating fragmentation. The decision fork is critical-bank containment versus broader banking value.
